content: Professor O. Mokuolu is affiliated with the Department of Paediatrics at the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital in Ilorin, Nigeria. Dr. D. Sinclair is part of the International Health Group at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom. Dr. L. Slutsker works at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, Georgia, USA. Dr. E. Tjitra is associated with the National Institute of Health and Development under the Ministry of Health in Jakarta, Indonesia. Dr. N. Valecha is a member of the National Institute of Malaria Research in New Delhi, India. Professor N. White, serving as co-chair, is part of the Faculty of Tropical Medicine at Mahidol University in Bangkok, Thailand. The sub-group on dose recommendations includes Professor K. Barnes (co-chair), Professor F. Binka, Dr. S. Lutalo, Dr. E. Juma, Professor O. Mokuolu, Dr. S. Parikh from the Department of Medicine at Yale University School of Public Health in Connecticut, USA, Dr. D. Sinclair, and Dr. J.J. Terlouw from the Malawi-Liverpool-Wellcome Trust Clinical Research Programme in Blantyre, Malawi. Professor N. White also serves as co-chair of this group. The Guideline Steering Group includes Dr. A. Bosman from the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland; Dr. K. Dhingra-Kumar from the Health Systems Policies and Workforce division at WHO in Geneva; Dr. M.E. Olumese, who serves as Secretary of the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva; Dr. F.C. Rietveld, Dr. P. Ringwald, Dr. M. Warsame, and Dr. W. Were, all of whom are part of the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva. Dr. W. Were also works in the Child and Adolescent Health division at WHO in Geneva. External reviewers for the WHO malaria guidelines include Dr. F. ter-Kuile from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom, Dr. R. McGready from the Shoklo Malaria Research Unit at Mahidol University in Bangkok, Thailand, and Professor F. Nosten from the same institution. Professor P. Garner from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom served as the guidelines methodologist. Participants in the technical consultation for the review of the malaria treatment guidelines and external expert reviewers declared relevant interests in accordance with WHO procedures. These interests were extensively discussed by the committee. While none of the declared interests were deemed to have direct relevance to the deliberations or recommendations of the meeting, panel members with declared interests were excluded from subcommittees on GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) and recommendations, as well as the drafting group. The declared interests were reviewed by WHO’s Legal Department. Dr. K. Barnes reported being a co-recipient of grants from the Medicines for Malaria Venture to conduct clinical trials evaluating antimalarial medicines. Dr. F. Binka disclosed membership in the INDEPTH network, which received a research grant from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation for Phase IV post-licensure studies on Euratesim. Dr. P. Garner reported receiving a grant from the UK Department for International Development to ensure global guidelines and decisions are based on reliable evidence. Dr. N. Valecha served as an investigator for a clinical trial supported by the Department of Science and Technology in India and Ranbaxy Laboratories Limited. No monetary benefits or conflicts of interest were identified in relation to this review. Professor N. White disclosed serving as an advisor to pharmaceutical companies developing new antimalarial medicines on a pro bono basis, without consultancy fees or remuneration. Members of the Guidelines Development Group (GDG) for 2022 included Dr. Dorothy Achu, Program Manager of the National Malaria Control Programme in Cameroon; Professor Karen Barnes, a clinical pharmacologist at the University of Cape Town in South Africa; Dr. Constance Bart-Plange, an independent malaria consultant in Ghana; Professor Adrianus Dondorp, Deputy Director of the Mahidol Oxford Tropical Medicine Research Unit in Thailand; and Professor Sanjeev Krishna, co-chair and expert in molecular parasitology and medicine at St. George’s University in London, United Kingdom. Professor Marcus Lacerda, an infectious disease researcher at the Tropical Medicine Foundation in Brazil, and Dr. Miriam Laufer, Director of the Office of Student Research at the University of Maryland School of Medicine in the USA, were also members. Professor Rose Leke, an immunology and parasitology expert at the University of Yaoundé in Cameroon, and Professor Olugbenga Mokuolu, co-chair and professor of paediatrics and child health at the University of Ilorin in Nigeria, contributed to the group. Professor Bernhards Ogutu, a senior clinical research scientist at the Kenya Medical Research Institute, and Professor Stephen Rogerson, an infectious diseases expert at the University of Melbourne in Australia, were also part of the GDG. Professor Philip Rosenthal from the University of California, USA, and Professor Terrie Taylor from Michigan State University, USA, were members as well. Professor Taylor disclosed serving on advisory boards for Novartis AG and receiving research funding from the US National Institutes of Health. These interests were deemed non-personal and non-specific, allowing her to participate in the group discussions. The Guidelines Steering Group (2022) included Andrea Bosman, Coordinator of the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva; Maurice Bucagu, from the Family, Women, Children, and Adolescents division at WHO in Geneva; Maria Bustos, Technical Officer for Malaria Control at WHO in Thailand; Jane Cunningham, Technical Officer at the Global Malaria Programme in Geneva; and Bayo Fatunmbi, Technical Officer for Malaria at WHO in Uganda. Elizabeth Juma from WHO Ghana, Roberto Montoya from WHO’s Regional Office for the Americas, and Deus Mubangizi, Coordinator for Prequalification Regulation and Access to Medicines at WHO in Geneva, were also members. Dr. Neena Valecha, Regional Malaria Adviser at WHO’s South-East Asia Regional Office in India, and Dr. Wilson Were, Medical Officer for Child Health and Development at WHO in Geneva, were part of the group. Dr. Ghasem Zamani, Regional Malaria Adviser at WHO’s Eastern Mediterranean Regional Office in Egypt, was also included. The External Review Group (ERG) for 2022 included Professor Ahmed Adeel, an independent consultant in the USA, and Professor Umberto d’Alessandro, Director of the Medical Research Council Unit in Gambia. The Systematic Review Team included Stephanie Dellicour, Martha Chaplin, and Paul Garner from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom, as well as Patricia Graves from the Australian Institute of Tropical Health and Medicine. Professor Karen Barnes declared her role at Oxford University’s Worldwide Antimalarial Resistance Network and her institution’s projects on antimalarial pharmacology funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the South African Ministry of Health. These interests were assessed as non-personal and non-specific. Professor Adrian Dondorp disclosed chairing the Malaria Advisory Council of Novartis since 2021 without remuneration. His group is currently studying the efficacy and safety of triple ACTs (artemisinin-based combination therapies) for uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with one of the ACTs provided for free by Fosun Pharma. These interests were deemed non-significant. Professor Marcus Lacerda declared institutional grants from the Medicines for Malaria Venture and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation to study the feasibility of radical cures for P. vivax malaria. These interests were also deemed non-significant.
